seo_description: Free, open-source macOS menu bar app that logs time spent in each thermal state daily and shows which apps were running when your Mac got hot.
hero_sub: HeatLedgerBar lives in your menu bar and records every change in your Mac's thermal state, then names the apps behind each hot period. Click the thermometer to see today at a glance.
features_sub: It tracks the official macOS thermal state over time instead of reading private temperature sensors.

features.title: Time in every thermal state
features.desc: Each change between nominal, fair, serious and critical is logged with timestamps. Today's stacked bar shows your share of time in each state.

features.title: Names the apps behind the heat
features.desc: While your Mac is at fair or worse, per-process CPU is sampled every 10 seconds. Each hot period lists the frontmost app and the heaviest apps.

features.title: 7 and 30 day history
features.desc: A history window charts time per state over 7 or 30 days, with a per-day table and the top culprit for each day.

features.title: Alerts when heat lingers
features.desc: Get a notification when your Mac stays hot for 5, 10 or 20 minutes, naming the heaviest app. You get at most one alert per hot period.

features.title: Thermometer in the menu bar
features.desc: The icon is tinted gray, yellow, orange or red to match the current thermal state, so you can check it without opening anything.

features.title: Local data, no network
features.desc: History is a JSON file on your Mac, kept for 7, 14 or 30 days. There are no accounts and nothing is sent anywhere.

permissions_step: When prompted, allow notifications so HeatLedgerBar can warn you about long hot periods (System Settings > Notifications); if you enable Launch at login, approve it under System Settings > General > Login Items.

faq.q: Is HeatLedgerBar free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is free, released under the MIT license, and the full source is on GitHub. If you find it useful, there is an optional Support button that opens a Ko-fi page.

Only notifications, which are optional and used for hot-Mac alerts, plus a login item if you turn on Launch at login. It does not ask for Accessibility, Screen Recording, Location or Full Disk Access.
In a JSON file at ~/Library/Application Support/HeatLedgerBar/ on your Mac. Nothing leaves your machine, and you can erase it at any time with Clear History in Settings.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account. Right-click the app and choose Open once to get past Gatekeeper, or build it yourself from source with Xcode.
